title: HyFiSS: A Hybrid Fidelity Stall-Aware Simulator for GPGPUs
problem: Cycle-accurate GPU simulators provide precise microarchitectural detail but suffer from slow simulation times and high computational overhead. Cycle-approximate simulators sacrifice accuracy for speed, creating a fundamental trade-off between performance prediction reliability and practical efficiency.
motivation: GPU simulators drive advancements in GPU architecture design and software optimization, but simulation bottlenecks and resource requirements limit their practical utility for research.
method: HyFiSS builds a detailed model of how a GPU's computing units execute code, tracking when and why they stall (pause waiting for memory or other resources). It uses actual scheduling logs to replay the thread scheduler's real decisions—how it ordered thread blocks (groups of threads) to run—rather than guessing them. To stay fast, it samples results at the thread-block level instead of simulating every cycle, and compresses instruction traces to reduce storage overhead while keeping simulation accurate.
key_novelty: By mixing precise tracking of GPU stalls with coarse thread-block-level sampling, it delivers cycle-accurate simulation precision with cycle-approximate simulation speed.
contributions: Hybrid fidelity GPU simulator achieving mean absolute percentage error comparable to Accel-Sim with 12.8× speedup
Fine-grained stall event tracking and attribution for precise bottleneck identification and performance analysis
Efficient SASS trace compression reducing storage by 3.2× compared to Accel-Sim and PPT-GPU
Thread block scheduler emulation using real-time logs enabling accurate simulation of GPU thread scheduling behavior
